newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU centrists hope to avoid special summit.
newsitem.headline: EU centrists hope to avoid special summit.

text.p: European Union centrist politicians said on Tuesday they hoped France's problem with the EMU stability pact could be overcome before an EU summit next week, but made clear an extra summit might be needed.

Meeting ahead of the EU summit in Amsterdam next Monday and Tuesday, leaders of the mainly Christian Democrat European People's Party said they believed the impasse in their plans caused by France could be sorted out by the end of the month.
"I hope the French find the courage to finalise their position before the Amsterdam summit," Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker told reporters as he arrived for the meeting.
But he added that he expected the problem would be solved by the time the Dutch hand over the EU presidency to Luxembourg on June 30.

At a meeting in Luxembourg on Monday, French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn told his EU partners that Paris needed time to study the stability pact, an integral part of plans for economic and monetary union (EMU).
He said the earliest date that the National Assembly could be consulted was June 19.
The pact, agreed in principle in Dublin in December, is designed to keep EU budgets in order after EMU is launched on January 1, 1999.
The European Commission is rushing to find a way to meet France's concerns, which revolve around its view that job creation should play a more important role in the EU's EMu plans.

Because employment is also an issue in the EU's negotiations on a new treaty, a number of officials have worried that the election of a new French government will mean that the treaty cannot be completed at Amsterdam.
Although most countries are pledged to finish the inter-governmental conference (IGC) talks next week, Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said another summit could not be ruled out.
"If we have to have a second meeting that is not a problem," he said as he arrived for the meeting. "We cannot rule out concluding the IGC a week later."
